title: Microsoft Teams: alternate text for images shared from OneDrive and SharePoint
summary: Hold: the messaging-policy path omits the Edit action needed to reach its settings. The feature description and rollout dates match Microsoft's notice and roadmap; licensing should state the published Teams requirement while keeping feature-specific licensing open.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans alternate text for images shared in Teams from OneDrive and SharePoint.
claims.quote: Improve accessibility by adding alternate text to images shared in Teams from OneDrive and SharePoint, helping users better understand visual content

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn does not yet describe this OneDrive and SharePoint image-alt-text feature.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Licensing is unknown because Microsoft has not published licensing specific to this change.
claims.quote: Except for joining Teams meetings anonymously, each user in your organization must have a Teams license before they can use Teams.
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to included. Replace licensing notes and the feature-licence gap wording in Cost and licensing, Open questions and the cost rationale with: 'Users need a Teams license to use Teams. Microsoft has not published a licensing requirement specific to this alt-text option.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/user-access.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Neither the roadmap record nor MC1523086 names a licence for this change.
claims.quote:
Who is affected:
- Microsoft 365 users who share or receive image attachments stored in OneDrive and SharePoint through Microsoft Teams.

claims.quote: Searched: Teams alternate text OneDrive SharePoint images licensing price prerequisites. Read the full Microsoft Teams Premium licensing page and its feature tables; no alternate-text image-attachment entry appears.

claims.where: controls[0].ui
claims.claim: Teams admin center > Messaging policies > policy > Edit sent messages is the route to the message-editing control.
claims.quote: In the left navigation of the Microsoft Teams admin center, go to Messaging policies. Select the policy by clicking to the left of the policy name, and then select Edit.
claims.fix: Replace controls[0].ui.path and the rendered table path with 'Messaging policies > policy > Edit > Edit sent messages'. Keep Teams admin center as the surface and https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/messaging-policies-in-teams as docs.

claims.where: controls[0].api
claims.claim: MicrosoftTeams PowerShell supports Set-CsTeamsMessagingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowUserEditMessage $true to enable editing one's own messages.
claims.quote: -AllowUserEditMessage: Determines whether a user is allowed to edit their own messages. Set this to TRUE to allow. Set this to FALSE to prohibit. -Identity: Identity for the teams messaging policy you're modifying.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance controls
claims.claim: Edit sent messages governs message editing in general, but its applicability to later image-description updates is not confirmed.
claims.quote: Edit sent messages - Use this setting to let users edit the messages that they sent in chat.
claims.fix: Replace the control note and its repeated caveat in Governance controls with: 'Existing control, not a separate alt-text switch. Edit sent messages lets users edit messages they sent in chat. MC1523086 describes later description updates as editing the sent message.' Keep the pilot-test advice without asserting undocumented field-specific behaviour.

claims.where: controls[1].ui and controls[1].api; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: No dedicated tenant or policy switch for alternate text on OneDrive and SharePoint images in Teams is documented on either admin UI or automation.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams alternate text OneDrive SharePoint images admin switch policy PowerShell; Set-CsTeamsMessagingPolicy Set-CsTeamsMessagingConfiguration alternate text image descriptions enable disable. Read messaging policy settings and both cmdlet syntaxes; no alt-text switch.

claims.quote: You can assign a policy directly to users, either individually or at scale through a batch assignment ... or to a group that the users are members of

claims.claim: A user can be assigned only one messaging policy at a time.
claims.quote: A user can only be assigned one messaging policy at a time.

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft's Teams accessibility guide for admins recommends sharing the guide on writing effective alt text.
claims.quote: Share the link how to write effective alt text with your organization to help users understand non-text messages shared in chat.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: Access to the shared image continues to depend on OneDrive and SharePoint file permissions.
claims.quote: Files shared within a conversation are automatically added to the document library, and permissions and file security options set in SharePoint are automatically reflected within Teams.
claims.fix: Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/limits-specifications-teams#storage for the existing file-permission boundary. Keep this about access to the original shared file, not access to the saved description.
